content: Calcium iodide (CaI2) is an ionic compound composed of calcium and iodine. It is highly soluble in water and exhibits deliquescent properties, meaning it can absorb moisture from the air and dissolve in it. This compound exists as a solid at room temperature and demonstrates the typical characteristics of an ionic halide. Due to its hygroscopic nature, calcium iodide must be stored in tightly-sealed containers to prevent it from absorbing moisture from the environment. In many ways, it shares similarities with calcium chloride. One of its applications is in the field of photography. Henri Moissan was the first to isolate pure calcium metal by reducing calcium iodide using pure sodium metal. Calcium iodide can also be synthesized by reacting calcium carbonate with hydroiodic acid. Over time, calcium iodide reacts slowly with oxygen and carbon dioxide present in the air, leading to the release of free iodine.
